leader.h1: Home renovations in Cape Town, built to last
leader.cta_line: Waterproofing, kitchens, bathrooms, painting and extensions. One team, one written scope, from the first site visit to the last snag.

home.intro_heading: What we do, and how we start
home.intro_body:
Cape Town houses are built for wind and winter rain, and most of the problems we are called out to fix started years ago at a junction nobody looked at. A parapet that was never flashed properly. A balcony that drains towards the wall instead of away from it. Plaster straight onto brick with no cavity, holding water against the inside face until the paint blisters.

We renovate the whole house, but we start at the water. Before we quote a bathroom or a kitchen we look at the roof above it, the walls beside it and the falls on the floor. That is why our quotes sometimes include work you did not ask for, and why they hold up once the job is done.

We work on houses and apartments across Cape Town, from 1950s Goodwood semis to newer family homes in Durbanville and Table View. One team takes the job from strip-out to snag list, and you get the scope, the material list and the sequence in writing before anything is demolished.
home.about_heading: A small Cape Town builder that starts with the water
home.about_body:
Plinth Renovations and Construction is based in Goodwood, on the northern side of Cape Town. We are a small company by design. The person who quotes your job is on site while it runs, and the trades on your job are people we work with every week rather than whoever is free that Monday.

Most of our work comes from owners who have already had one bad experience. A leak that was painted over. A shower tiled without a fall to the drain. A quote that grew once the walls were open. So we do the unglamorous part first. We open the ceiling, read the moisture, and tell you what the water is doing before we sell you a finish.

We are also honest about scope. If a repair will hold, we say so instead of quoting a rebuild. If the waterproofing under your tiles has already failed, we tell you that new tiles will not save it.

## How a job runs

- A site visit, at your home, at a time that suits you
- A written estimate that separates what is essential from what is optional
- A sequence you can plan around, and a single point of contact
- Daily clean-up, and a snag list we work through with you at the end
home.services_intro: Eight services, one crew, one written scope. Most jobs combine two or three of them: a bathroom that needs waterproofing first, a kitchen that needs a wall moved, an exterior that needs plaster and paint before the winter rain arrives.
home.areas_body:
We are based in Goodwood and work within roughly 25 km of it: the Northern Suburbs, the City Bowl, the Atlantic Seaboard and the Southern Suburbs. Stellenbosch and Somerset West we take on by arrangement, when the job is large enough to justify the travel.

Our area pages cover the suburbs where we do most of our work. If yours is not listed, ask. The answer is usually yes.

The crew that strips your bathroom is the crew that waterproofs it, tiles it and hands it back.

Sheeting, daily clean-up and a plan for the kitchen or bathroom your family still has to use.

faq.q: How much does a renovation cost in Cape Town?
faq.a: It depends on the scope, and anyone who quotes you a firm price per square metre before seeing the house is guessing. We visit, measure, open what needs opening, then give you one written estimate with the essential work and the optional work separated.

faq.q: Do you handle waterproofing and damp as part of a renovation?
faq.a: Yes, and we treat it as the first job rather than a line item at the end. A bathroom or kitchen quote that ignores the roof above it is a quote we would not sign off on ourselves.

faq.q: How long does a bathroom or kitchen take?
faq.a: We give you a date range in the written quote, based on the actual scope. We do not publish a standard number, because a bathroom that needs a drain moved is a different job from one that does not.

faq.q: Do you take on small jobs?
faq.a: Yes. A leaking parapet, one room painted, a ceiling patch, a single shower that has to be redone. Small jobs are often how we meet the owners we later build for.

faq.q: Do you work outside Cape Town?
faq.a: Stellenbosch and Somerset West by arrangement for larger jobs. Our normal working radius is about 25 km around Goodwood.

faq.q: Do I need plans or council approval?
faq.a: Structural work, alterations and additions usually need approval from the City of Cape Town before work starts. We tell you when it applies to your job, and we can work with your architect or draughtsman.

faq.q: Can I stay in the house while you work?
faq.a: Usually yes. We sheet off the work area, plan around the bathroom or kitchen you still need, and clean up at the end of each day.
Staged against progress and set out in the quote before we start. We do not ask for the whole job upfront.

services.name: Waterproofing
services.title_tag: Waterproofing Cape Town | Roof, Balcony and Wall Repairs
services.meta_description: Waterproofing in Cape Town for roofs, parapets, balconies, box gutters and basements. We find where the water enters before we quote. Free site visit.

leader.cta_line: Most leaks are not in the middle of the roof. They are at a junction, a parapet or a balcony edge that was never detailed properly. We start there.

services.intro_heading: Where Cape Town roofs actually leak
services.intro_body:
Cape Town's rain arrives with a north-westerly front that pushes water sideways across roofs and up under tiles. That is why so many leaks here are nowhere near the middle of the roof. They are at the upstand where a flat roof meets a wall, in the box gutter that has silted up, behind the flashing around a chimney, or at the edge of a balcony where the membrane was laid over a dirty surface.

Waterproofing fails in two ways. The material itself reaches the end of its life, which is predictable. Or the detail was wrong from the start, which is not, and it is the far more common of the two. A membrane laid without a proper primer, a fall that runs back towards the wall, a tile roof re-flashed with sealant instead of lead. You can redo the surface every year and still have a leak, because the water never entered where the surface is.

So we work from the water's point of view. We get into the ceiling void, read moisture through the plaster, and where it is not obvious we run a hose test on the suspect area and watch what happens inside. Only then do we specify a system, because the right answer on a fibre-cement roof is not the right answer on a concrete slab, and neither is the right answer on a wall that has to stay breathable.
services.detail_intro: Every one of these is a different substrate and a different detail. We treat them as separate jobs rather than one product applied everywhere.

If water has reached the ceiling, the plaster and insulation may need replacing as well. We price that separately and only if it is needed.

services.name: Damp Proofing
services.title_tag: Damp Proofing Cape Town | Rising Damp and Wall Repair
services.meta_description: Damp proofing in Cape Town. Rising damp, penetrating damp and condensation diagnosed properly, then treated at the source. Free written estimate.

leader.cta_line: Rising damp, penetrating damp and condensation look similar on a wall and need completely different repairs. Getting the diagnosis right is most of the job.

services.intro_heading: Three kinds of damp, three different repairs
services.intro_body:
Damp is a symptom, not a diagnosis. The same bubbling paint and tide mark at skirting height can come from groundwater rising through a failed damp course, from rain entering a wall from outside, or from warm air condensing on a cold internal surface. Treat the wrong one and the damp returns within a season, which is why so many owners end up repainting the same wall every year.

Rising damp is groundwater moving up through the brickwork because the original damp proof course has failed, been bridged by a later concrete path or patio, or was never there. It stops at roughly a metre and leaves a horizontal tide mark. Penetrating damp comes in from outside: a cracked render, a failed window seal, a leaking gutter soaking the wall head, or a plinth that sits below the external ground level. Condensation is different again, and common in Cape Town's older houses where windows have been sealed and heating added without any ventilation.

We identify which one you have before quoting. That means moisture readings at different heights, a look at the external ground level and drainage, and a check on how the room is ventilated and heated.
services.detail_intro: Each of these needs its own method. A chemical injection will not fix a leaking gutter, and a coat of sealant will not fix rising damp.

subitems.name: Rising damp
subitems.desc: Damp course injection, plus removal of the plaster that has absorbed salts, replaced with a salt-resistant render.

subitems.name: Penetrating damp
subitems.desc: Found on the outside and repaired there: render, sealant, flashings, sills and the ground level against the wall.

subitems.name: Condensation and mould
subitems.desc: Ventilation, extraction and surface treatment. Mould is a symptom of moist air, not of a leaking wall.

subitems.name: Bridged damp course
subitems.desc: Paths, patios and paving laid above the damp course, cut back and detailed so the wall can dry.

subitems.name: Salt-damaged plaster
subitems.desc: Contaminated plaster removed to a sound base and replaced with a render that tolerates salt.

subitems.name: Plinth and foundation level
subitems.desc: The base of the wall where ground water sits against the structure, including the plinth detail many older Cape homes rely on.

cost.heading: What changes the price of damp repair
rows: Which damp it is
A condensation problem needs ventilation. Rising damp needs a damp course and new plaster. The costs are not comparable.
Length of affected wall
Injection and replastering are priced by the metre of wall treated, inside and out.
Access to the base
Paving, patios and planted beds against the wall have to be opened or cut back to treat it properly.
Internal finish
If the plaster has to come off, the skirting, paint and sometimes the floor finish come with it.
Whether the outside is the cause
Fixing the external detail is often the cheaper half and the only one that lasts.
cost.note: We diagnose first and quote the repair that matches the cause. If a cheaper repair will genuinely hold, we will price that instead.

steps.detail: Moisture readings at several heights and positions to establish the pattern.
Ground levels, drainage, render condition, sills, gutters and any later addition bridging the damp course.
Which damp it is, what is causing it and what the repair involves, before any work is priced.
Injection, external repair, drainage or ventilation, depending on what the diagnosis says.
Salt-resistant render where needed, and a return visit to confirm the wall is drying.

Most damp repairs fail because only the inside was treated. We price both sides.
Contaminated plaster comes off and goes back with a render that tolerates salt, not standard skim.
A drying wall tells you whether the repair worked. We come back and read it.

services.name: Painting
services.title_tag: Painting Contractors Cape Town | Interior and Exterior
services.meta_description: Painting contractors in Cape Town for interiors, exteriors, roofs and kitchen cabinets. Proper surface preparation before a coat goes on. Free estimate.

leader.eyebrow: Painting and surface preparation, Cape Town
leader.cta_line: Paint is the last five percent of a painting job. The other ninety-five is preparation, and it is where most repaints fail.

services.intro_heading: Why repaints fail in one season
services.intro_body:
A coat of paint over a damp wall will blister. Paint over chalky, powdery plaster will peel in sheets. Paint over a crack that is still moving will crack again, in the same line, within months. None of these are paint problems. They are preparation problems, and Cape Town's coastal air and winter rain find every one of them.

We prepare before we paint. That means washing and degreasing, scraping back anything loose, cutting out cracks and filling them with something that can move, sealing bare plaster with the right primer, and only then applying a system matched to the surface. On exterior work it also means waiting for the wall to be dry, which in winter can mean rescheduling a day rather than painting wet masonry and hoping.

We also do the work that sits between painting and building: repairing blown plaster, replacing rotten window beads, re-puttying glass, sealing joints that have opened, and coating roofs that are sound but have lost their protection.
services.detail_intro: The surface decides the system. Enamel on a wall that needs a breathable coating is a mistake that shows up in the first wet winter.

A sound wall takes two coats. A wall with blown plaster, cracks and old enamel takes days before the first coat.
Surface area and height

Coating system
A standard acrylic, a breathable mineral paint and a roof membrane are three different products at three price points.
Number of colours
Feature walls, ceilings in a different colour and trim all add cutting-in time.
What is being moved
Furniture, blinds, air conditioners and light fittings all have to come down or be protected.

leader.cta_line: A kitchen is a plumbing job, an electrical job and a carpentry job in the same room. The order they happen in decides how it turns out.

services.intro_heading: The sequence matters more than the finish
services.intro_body:
Most kitchen renovations that go wrong were not let down by the cabinets. They were let down by the order of work. A new layout decided after the plumbing was moved. A stone top templated before the cabinets were level. An extractor chosen before anyone checked where the duct could go. Tiling started before the electrical second fix, so the sockets ended up in the wrong place.

We plan the sequence before demolition. That means agreeing the layout and the appliance list, marking the services, confirming what can move and what should stay, and writing all of it down. Only then do we strip the room.

We work with your design if you have one, and we will tell you honestly when a layout will cost more than it is worth because of where the waste pipe or the distribution board sits. If you do not have a design, we will plan a practical layout with you: working triangle, landing space beside the oven and fridge, and enough counter where you actually prepare food.

services.name: Bathroom Renovations
services.title_tag: Bathroom Renovations Cape Town | Waterproofed and Tiled
services.meta_description: Bathroom renovations in Cape Town with the waterproofing done properly: falls to the drain, flood-tested membranes and tiling that lasts. Free estimate.

leader.cta_line: A bathroom is a waterproofing job with tiles on top. If the layer under the tiles is wrong, the finish does not matter.

services.intro_heading: The part you cannot see is the whole job
services.intro_body:
Most failed bathrooms in Cape Town fail the same way. Water gets behind the tiles, sits on the slab or in the wall, and finds the ceiling of the room below. By the time the paint blisters downstairs, the damage has been happening for months. Retiling over a failed waterproofing membrane is the single most common way owners spend money twice.

So the sequence we insist on is: strip the room back to the structure, repair whatever the water has damaged, fall the floor to the drain, waterproof the floor and the wet walls, flood test it, and only then tile. The flood test is not optional for us. Filling the floor with water and leaving it there tells you whether the membrane is sound before it disappears under tile.

We also look at the things that make a bathroom work after the photos are taken: where the water goes when the shower is running, whether the extractor actually vents outside, whether the door clears the new floor level, and whether there is somewhere to put a towel that is not the back of a chair.

services.intro_heading: What a full renovation actually involves
services.intro_body:
A whole-house renovation is not one big job. It is a dozen jobs that have to happen in the right order, and the order is what separates a smooth project from a house that is open for months. Structural work before services. Services before closing walls. Waterproofing before finishes. Finishes before the snag list.

Cape Town's housing stock makes this more interesting than it sounds. A 1950s Goodwood house has solid brick walls, no cavity and a damp course that may or may not still work. A 1970s Bellville house may have been extended twice, each time with a roof tied into the last one. A newer Durbanville home has modern services but detailing at parapets and balconies that was value-engineered at construction.

We plan around the structure you actually have. Sometimes that means keeping a wall that a plan said to remove, because it is carrying more than the drawing showed. Sometimes it means opening a room differently to avoid moving a drain. We will always tell you which is which, and what each option costs, before demolition starts.

services.name: Plastering
services.title_tag: Plastering Cape Town | Skimming, Cracks and Cornices
services.meta_description: Plastering in Cape Town: skimming, crack repair, cornices, external plaster and plasterboard ceilings. Surface prepared properly before paint.

leader.eyebrow: Plastering and surface repair, Cape Town
leader.cta_line: A wall is only as good as the plaster under the paint. Cracks, hollow patches and blown render all start here.

services.intro_heading: Fix the plaster, or paint it twice
services.intro_body:
Plaster fails in Cape Town for reasons that are usually visible once you know what to look for. Movement cracks follow the line of a lintel or a joint between two materials. Hollow-sounding patches mean the plaster has lost its bond to the brick behind it. Powdering, salt-stained plaster at low level means moisture is coming through the wall, and no amount of skim will hold it.

We treat plaster as a repair job before a finishing job. Cracks are opened, not filled. Hollow plaster is cut back to sound material, not skimmed over. Where damp is the cause, the source is fixed before the wall is re-plastered, and where the wall needs to breathe we use a render that lets it.

For interior work, skimming an old wall flat is often the fastest way to make a room feel new without touching the structure. For exteriors, the priorities are different: weather resistance, crack control and a finish that can take the wind and the sun.
services.detail_intro: Interior and exterior, new work and repair, including the ceilings and mouldings that usually need attention at the same time.

cost.heading: What changes the price of plastering
rows: Repair or replace
Skimming a sound wall is quick. Cutting out and replacing blown plaster is not.
Height and access
Double volumes and stairwells need scaffolding, which costs as much as the plastering.
What is on the wall
Old enamel, wallpaper glue and multiple paint layers all have to be removed before new plaster will bond.
Matching existing
Cornice profiles and textured finishes take time to match, and sometimes a mould has to be made.
Drying time
New plaster has to dry before paint. Rushing it is how you get a finish that fails in the first winter.
cost.note: We price plastering per wall or per room after seeing the surface, and we tell you when plaster is not the real problem.

steps.detail: Tap for hollow areas, check crack patterns, and establish whether moisture is involved.
Cut back unsound plaster, open cracks, remove failed coatings and key the surface.
Where damp or movement is behind the failure, that is dealt with before new plaster goes on.
Base coat and finish coat applied to the right thickness, with corners and reveals set true.
Sanded, checked under light and handed over dry, so the painter is not correcting our work.

whyus.point: We cut back, not cover up
whyus.detail: Hollow plaster is removed to a sound base, so the repair does not fail beside the patch.
Plastering over a damp wall is a waste of both our time and your money.
Existing profiles reproduced rather than replaced with a near-enough modern section.
We hand over a surface that takes paint properly, not one that needs sanding by someone else.

services.name: Home Extensions
services.title_tag: Home Extensions Cape Town | Additions and Extra Rooms
services.meta_description: Home extensions in Cape Town: extra rooms, open-plan additions and covered patios, with the roof tie-in and waterproofing detailed properly.

leader.cta_line: An extension is judged by the join. Where the new roof meets the old one is where most of them fail.

services.intro_heading: The join decides whether it lasts
services.intro_body:
Adding a room is straightforward in principle: foundations, walls, a roof, and a hole in the existing house to connect the two. What decides whether the extension is still sound in ten years is the detailing at the junction, and that is the part that gets rushed.

A new roof tied into an old one needs the flashing to be rebuilt, not sealed. A new slab meeting an old wall needs the damp course to be continuous, or the old wall starts drawing water from the new floor. A new opening in an existing wall needs a lintel of the right size and bearing, and the wall above it supported while the opening is formed.

We build extensions as structural work first and finishes second. Where the City of Cape Town requires plans and approval, we work with your architect or draughtsman, or tell you what needs to be submitted before we start. We would rather delay a start than build something that has to be undone.
services.detail_intro: From a single extra room to a full-width addition, including the outdoor rooms that Cape Town houses always end up wanting.

cost.heading: What changes the price of an extension
rows: Ground conditions
Slope, rock and old foundations all change the excavation and the foundation design.
The junction
A simple lean-to roof against a wall is cheaper than tying a new pitched roof into an existing one.
Approvals
Plans, engineer input and council submission add cost and time before the first brick.
Services
Extending water, waste, power and drainage to the new room is often underestimated.
Finishes
Matching the existing house costs more than making the extension obviously new.

Working with your draughtsman or architect on submission to the City of Cape Town where required.

New roof, tie-in to the existing roof, flashings, and the extension closed before finishes begin.

areas.name: Durbanville
areas.title_tag: Renovations Durbanville | Waterproofing and Home Renovations
areas.meta_description: Renovations and waterproofing in Durbanville. Older town-centre homes and newer estates, with wind-driven rain on the western walls. Free written estimate.

leader.cta_line: From the older homes around the town centre to the estates off the wine route, we repair the water first and renovate after.

areas.intro_heading: Durbanville homes, and what the weather does to them
areas.intro_body:
Durbanville sits high and open on the northern edge of the city, which is good for views and hard on walls. The north-westerly front that comes through in winter drives rain almost horizontally into west and north-facing facades, and any crack in the plaster or gap around a window becomes an entry point rather than a cosmetic problem.

The older houses near the town centre were built with plaster on brick, often with a damp course that has since failed. That shows up as rising damp at skirting level, paint that bubbles back within a season, and a smell in the rooms that face the ground. Newer estates have the opposite problem: the waterproofing is recent but the detailing at parapets, balconies and roof junctions is where it leaks.

We work on both. That includes single-storey family homes in Vierlanden and Goedemoed, townhouse complexes where the body corporate needs a scope it can approve, and older properties where the renovation has to respect a structure worth keeping.

whyus.point: We know which walls take the weather
whyus.detail: North-west facing facades and parapets in Durbanville are where we look first, before anything cosmetic.
Written scopes, clear access arrangements and no surprises for neighbours in a complex.
The same crew from strip-out to snag list, within about 25 km of our Goodwood base.

areas.cta_subtext: Book a free site visit in Durbanville and get a written estimate before anything is opened up.

areas.name: Bellville
areas.title_tag: Renovations Bellville | Waterproofing and Home Renovations
areas.meta_description: Home renovations, damp repair and waterproofing in Bellville. Older plaster-on-brick homes around Voortrekker Road and the northern suburbs. Free estimate.

leader.h1: Renovations and damp repair in Bellville
leader.cta_line: Bellville has some of the best-built older houses in the city, and some of the most tired waterproofing. We fix both.

areas.intro_heading: Older Bellville homes need diagnosis, not a coat of paint
areas.intro_body:
Much of Bellville was built between the 1950s and the 1980s, in solid brick with thick plaster and no cavity. It is a good way to build a house, and it means a wall that gets wet stays wet for a long time. When the damp course at the base fails, the moisture has nowhere to go but up into the plaster, and out through your skirting board.

We see the same three problems in Bellville again and again. Rising damp at ground level, especially on the side that gets no sun. Penetrating damp around windows and under sills where the sealant has aged out. And roof leaks at the junction between the original house and a later addition, which is almost always where a previous builder tied a new roof into an old one without redoing the flashing.

Repainting over any of those buys you one season. We test the moisture, find where it enters, and treat the cause before we quote the cosmetic work.

whyus.detail: Moisture readings and a hose test tell us whether it is rising damp, penetration or condensation.
Thick plaster, no cavity, old plumbing and wiring. We work with what is there instead of pretending it is new.
Bellville is close to Goodwood, so site visits and call-backs are easy to schedule.

areas.cta_subtext: Get a written estimate for your Bellville home, including a proper look at where the damp is coming from.

areas.name: Parow
areas.title_tag: Renovations Parow | Waterproofing, Damp Repair and Painting
areas.meta_description: Renovations, waterproofing and damp repair in Parow. Older homes around Parow North and East, plus garages and carports. Free written estimate.

leader.cta_line: Solid older houses, long-standing damp and roofs that have been patched more than once. We start again from the detail.

areas.intro_body:
Parow North and Parow East hold some of the most practical family houses in the northern suburbs. Bigger plots, solid walls, and garages or carports that have often been added later and tied into the original structure with less care than the house itself was built with.

That is usually where the trouble is. A carport roof that meets the house wall without a proper flashing. A garage conversion where the original outside wall was never damp-proofed before it became an inside wall. A flat roof over a back room that has been patched with whatever was available and now holds water in the corners.

We work on the whole envelope. Roof, flashings, parapets, external plaster, then the inside: ceilings, paint, tiles, and the joinery that water damage usually takes with it.

whyus.detail: Most leaks at an added garage or carport are a flashing detail. We rebuild it properly rather than sealing over it.
Cracks and blown plaster are cut back and repaired before painting, not filled and painted over.
Parow is minutes from our Goodwood base, so site visits do not cost you a call-out fee.

areas.cta_subtext: Ask for a free site visit in Parow. We will show you where the water is getting in.

areas.name: Table View
areas.title_tag: Renovations Table View | Waterproofing and Coastal Home Repairs
areas.meta_description: Renovations and waterproofing in Table View. Salt air, west-facing walls and balconies that take the wind. Free written estimate from a Cape Town team.

leader.h1: Renovations and waterproofing in Table View
leader.cta_line: Sea-facing walls, balconies and roofs take more punishment here than anywhere else in the city. We build for that.

areas.intro_heading: Coastal air changes what a renovation needs
areas.intro_body:
Table View and the Bloubergstrand strip face the Atlantic, which means salt, wind and driving rain on the same wall. Metal corrodes faster, sealant fails sooner, and any fixing that was not specified for coastal conditions shows it within a couple of winters.

We see the results constantly. Balcony waterproofing that has lifted at the edge. Window frames with rust bleeding through the paint. Wall ties and lintels that have been quietly corroding behind the plaster. Roof sheets and fixings that have reached the end of their life on the sea side of the house while the land side still looks fine.

Coastal work is not about using a different product on the same detail. It is about specifying the right one, in the right sequence, and accepting that the west elevation will always need more attention than the east.

whyus.detail: Fixings, membranes and coatings chosen for salt exposure, not the cheapest option on the shelf.
Falls, upstands and edge details rebuilt so water leaves the structure instead of sitting on it.

whyus.point: We tell you what can wait
whyus.detail: Not every rust mark means a rebuild. We separate the urgent from the cosmetic in writing.

areas.cta_subtext: Free site visit in Table View or Blouberg, including a look at the sea-facing side of the house.

areas.name: Brackenfell
areas.title_tag: Renovations Brackenfell | Extensions, Waterproofing and Kitchens
areas.meta_description: Home renovations, extensions and waterproofing in Brackenfell. Family homes, added rooms and ageing roofs. Free written estimate from Plinth.

leader.cta_line: Growing families, added rooms and roofs that were built for a smaller house. We make the extension fit the original.

areas.intro_body:
Brackenfell grew fast, and a lot of the housing stock has been added to over the years: a room at the back, a covered patio, a garage that became a flatlet. Each addition is a new roof meeting an old one, a new slab meeting an old wall, and a new waterproofing detail that someone had to get right.

When it goes wrong, the symptoms appear somewhere else. A damp patch in the middle of a bedroom ceiling that traces back to a patio roof two rooms away. A cold spot and a smell in a converted garage whose floor was never sealed. A wall that cracks because the new lintel and the old wall are moving differently.

We treat an extension as a structural problem before a cosmetic one: how the new work ties in, how water leaves the junction, and how the old wall dries. Then we finish it so you cannot see where the old house ends.

whyus.detail: Flashings, lintels and movement joints at the junction decide whether an extension lasts.

whyus.point: One team for the whole job
whyus.detail: Foundations, walls, roof, waterproofing, ceilings and finishes from the same crew.
We phase the work so the house stays usable while it happens.

areas.cta_subtext: Talk to us about your Brackenfell extension or renovation. Free site visit, written estimate.

areas.name: Southern Suburbs
areas.title_tag: Renovations Southern Suburbs | Waterproofing and Home Renovations
areas.meta_description: Renovations, damp repair and waterproofing across Cape Town's Southern Suburbs, from Rondebosch to Tokai. Older homes handled with care. Free estimate.

leader.h1: Renovations in Cape Town's Southern Suburbs
leader.cta_line: Older, higher-value homes where the detail matters and the original structure is worth protecting.

areas.intro_body:
The Southern Suburbs hold some of Cape Town's oldest residential stock: Victorian and Edwardian cottages in Wynberg and Plumstead, 1930s family homes in Rondebosch and Claremont, and larger properties up against the mountain in Tokai and Constantia.

Old houses have specific problems. Soft brick and lime plaster that must not be sealed with a modern waterproof coating, or the wall cannot breathe and the damp moves inward. Concrete floors laid without a membrane. Gutters and downpipes sized for a smaller roof, now asked to carry a bigger one. Window openings that were never flashed because the original detail relied on a generous overhang that a later alteration removed.

The work here is often careful rather than large: matching original mouldings, repairing rather than replacing, and choosing materials that let an old wall dry the way it was designed to.

whyus.detail: We choose renders and coatings that let masonry dry, instead of trapping moisture behind a sealed surface.
Cornices, skirtings and trims matched to the original rather than replaced with whatever is in stock.

whyus.point: We protect what is worth keeping
whyus.detail: Repair is quoted alongside replacement so you can see the real cost of both.

areas.cta_subtext: Request a free site visit in the Southern Suburbs and a written estimate that separates repair from replacement.
